text: the one thing i dont like so much is i am able to click on edges i cant even see (they are on the other side of a model) and same for verts
resolution: Occlusion-aware vertex/edge picking — you can no longer click a vertex or edge on the far side of the model that you can't see. Root cause: pickVertex/pickEdge were pure screen-nearest projections, blind to whether the surface hid the element. Added model_paint.occluded(cam, p): casts a ray from the eye to p and returns hidden when a FRONT-facing triangle lies in front of it (the renderer culls back faces, so only front faces visibly occlude; a scale-relative eps tolerates a vertex sitting on its own incident faces). pickVertex tests the vertex point, pickEdge tests the edge midpoint, and both run the test only for in-radius candidates that beat the current best, so a click costs just a handful of O(faces) raycasts (same order as a paint dab, never per-frame) — no fps regression. Unit-tested in model_paint (point behind a front face = occluded; on-surface and in-front = visible); both test-model-paint and test-mesh-edit green; built clean; render unchanged (dots still show back verts faintly, Blockbench-style — you SEE them but only pick visible ones). KNOWN: the live marquee still selects through hidden elements (kept fast; per-move occlusion would raycast every boxed element each move) — can add occlusion-on-release if the user wants marquee to match.
